item.title: Manish Tewari | Will India Pause Or Retreat On Chabahar?
item.description: A shift began in 2016, when India entered into an agreement with Iran and Afghanistan — aimed at building the port along with linked transportation routes. Money flowed heavily from India, covering close to 120 million dollars just for upgrading the port, while also offering more lending tools for cross-border infrastructure work. Instead of outside firms, Indian entities like India Ports Global Limited took charge of running the terminal
